newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine police say HK drug suspect's name spurious.
newsitem.headline: Philippine police say HK drug suspect's name spurious.

text.p: Philippine police said on Thursday that a Chinese man they had arrested in one of the country's biggest drug seizures in 20 years had apparently faked his identity.
"It appears that he was using a fictitious name," national police spokesman Colonel Enrique Galang told Reuters.
National police chief General Recaredo Sarmiento identified the suspect on Wednesday as a Hong Kong resident named Wai Kuen Alan Tong, 31.
But Hong Kong police found the real Alan Tong at home in Hong Kong -- minus his government-issued identity card which had been stolen.

Philippine police said they based the name of the suspect on a Hong Kong identity card he was carrying when police arrested him in Cavite province south of Manila and seized $25 million worth of morphine and metamphetamine stimulants.

"Definitely we could not be referring to the Tong in Hong Kong because he is in Hong Kong. We were only referring to the man we caught here," Cavite chief investigator Major Leo Santiago said by telephone.
Santiago said the suspect had no passport. His only identification was the Hong Kong resident's card in his wallet. The man had refused to talk when questioned by police, he added.
"We can determine his real identity through liaison with the Hong Kong police," Santiago said.
Galang said the suspect may have assumed the name Alan Tong "... to hide his real identity. Our investigation is continuing."
"The reason criminals change their names is because they know that worldwide there is an exchange of information among law enforcement agencies," Galang added.
Philippine police said the drug seizure was probably the country's biggest in 20 years.
